source.alpha_convention: Theorem2.2 invokes alpha-convex without restating its sign. Definition1.5 defines this only for alpha>=0; alpha0 is convex/nonexpansive, alpha>0 strongly convex/contractive. Arbitrary real alpha is not the literal source domain.
source.statement: For two supplied gradient flows of the same alpha-convex objective, norm(Yt-Xt)<=exp(-alpha*t)*norm(Y0-X0), all t>=0.
source.proof: Differentiate squared distance, apply gradient monotonicity (1.5), then Gronwall with coefficient-2alpha and take the nonnegative square root.
source.background: Source Section2 assumes C2 f and does not prove gradient-flow well-posedness. Global attained-minimum convention is irrelevant to this two-trajectory estimate.

proof_route: Set D(t)=Y(t)-X(t) and derive actual right derivative -(gradient f(Yt)-gradient f(Xt)).
Use HasDerivWithinAt.norm_sq; rewrite inner product using real symmetry/signs.
Apply existing gradient_inner_lower_bound_of_strongConvexOn atXt,Yt to obtain squared-distance derivative<=-2alpha*norm(Dt)^2.
Feed actual right slope and closed-interval continuity to existing scalar Gronwall.
Rewrite exp(-2alpha*t)=exp(-alpha*t)^2, use positivity and nonnegative norms to pass from squared estimate to requested norm estimate.

test_recommendation.main: f(x)=x²/2; X(t)=exp(-t), Y(t)=2exp(-t). Prove both actual derivatives and gradient, apply result at positive times on arbitrary finite horizon, and check sharp equality. Neither curve is stationary and initial distance1 is positive.

test_recommendation.robustness: Using squared distance rather than differentiating norm avoids any hidden nonzero-separation hypothesis when trajectories meet.
